subject: SaaS Summit — lead-capture offline resync & HubSpot mapping
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: SaaS Summit — lead-capture offline resync & HubSpot mapping

Team — quick kickoff for the badge-scanner/lead-capture plan at SaaS Summit (June 10-12). Two priorities: 1) robust offline capture + resync behavior when booths lose connectivity, and 2) a clean HubSpot ingestion schema with consent captured at scan time.

I attached a first-pass mapping (hubspot-field-mapping-v1.csv) and a short consent snippet for legal review. High-level asks:
- Confirm max offline queue the Badgetech devices can hold and resync window (hours after connectivity restored).
- Confirm the fallback CSV export format if the live API fails (we'll upload to a secure bucket).
- Finalize HubSpot field names, dedupe rules, and the campaign attribution plan.
- Decide who owns firmware push for scanner fleet (we need v2.1 applied before the show).

Proposed owners: Marissa -> HubSpot mapping + test import; Laura -> onsite ops and device staging; Neha -> privacy/consent approval; Connor -> vendor technical contact + firmware.

I want a short playbook by June 1 that we can hand to the onsite lead. Can you each reply with quick confirmations and any blockers?

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hubspot-field-mapping-v1.csv (CSV stub), consent-snippet-v1.docx (docx stub)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-30T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: SaaS Summit — lead-capture offline resync & HubSpot mapping

Ben — looping in the latest from BadgeTech support (pasted below). Short takeaway: devices hold ~10k scans offline, resync via Wi-Fi/cellular when back online, and they can push an S3 export every 6 hours if our HubSpot API is flaky. Firmware v2.1 is required for "graceful resync" (it preserves timestamp order and includes CRC).

Forwarded message from BadgeTech Support:
> From: BadgeTech Support <support@badgetech.io>
> Date: 2027-05-30T11:30:00Z
> To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
> Subject: Re: resync window and exports
>
> Hi Connor — confirmed:
> - Offline queue: 10,000 records per device (circular buffer); older than buffer will be dropped.
> - Resync: automatic when connectivity returns; default retry window is 72 hours but we can set a 48h SLA for resync attempts.
> - Exports: S3 dump every 6 hours (JSON lines) + POST to a configurable ingestion endpoint (supports basic auth / API key).
> - Firmware v2.1: fixes ordering and adds an incremental resume token for partial resync.
>
> I'll attach the resync schema and a short integration guide. Let me know if you want a test device shipped.
>
> — BadgeTech Support

Connor
Technical Events Lead

Attachments referenced: resync-schema.json (schema stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-31T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SaaS Summit — lead-capture offline resync & HubSpot mapping

Thanks Connor — good notes. I reviewed the mapping and made a few edits (see attached csv). Key items:
- HubSpot target properties: email, firstname, lastname, company, job_title, phone, lead_source (SaaS Summit), campaign, badge_id, scan_timestamp_utc, consent_text, consent_method.
- Deduping logic: primary by email; fallback by badge_id when email missing. Import should upsert on email and set contact creation to keep original created_at when present.
- Consent text: suggested copy to include in UI and on the scanner export. Short version (for badge scan preview):
  "By scanning your badge you consent to receive communications from Redwood Inference and its partners. You can opt out at any time. Privacy policy: https://redwood.com/privacy."

Legal flag (Neha) — I redlined the snippet to add a checkbox reference for EU attendees. We should capture consent_method = 'badge_scan' or 'form'.

Operational notes:
- If BadgeTech provides the S3 exports, we'll consume them via a short lambda that writes to a staging HubSpot import CSV every 6 hours.
- If live POST fails, we fallback to S3 -> secure bucket -> manual import.

I'll take ownership of the HubSpot import tests this week. Laura, please confirm how many devices you'll stage and whether you want the firmware pushed centrally or applied during device provisioning.

Marissa Cole
Field Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: hubspot-field-mapping-v1.csv (updated)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: BadgeTech Support <support@badgetech.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaS Summit <events@saas-summit.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T02:00:00Z
Subject: Action plan & weekend firmware window — please acknowledge

BadgeTech + team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Consolidated plan and asks (please ACK inline):

1) Firmware push: schedule v2.1 rollout to 25 devices. Proposed maintenance window: 2027-06-03 02:00-04:00 UTC (overnight local). Connor to coordinate with BadgeTech for OTA.
2) Offline queue: set to 48h resync attempts (BadgeTech to confirm). Devices with >10k samples: flag and swap during staging.
3) HubSpot ingestion: Marissa to run test imports; pipeline: POST -> staging lambda -> HubSpot import. If POST fails, rely on S3 exports every 6h for manual import.
4) Consent: use Marissa's approved snippet with EU checkbox; Neha to sign off by EOD 6/1.
5) Onsite ops: Laura to handle device swap, power checks, and badge-disposal policy (no PII left on device).

Deliverables before June 6:
- Test import of 500 synthetic records into our HubSpot demo account (Marissa)
- Firmware pushed to 3 test devices and validation that resync order is preserved (Connor + BadgeTech)
- DPA link and S3 bucket ACLs in place (Ben will chase BadgeTech legal)

BadgeTech — can you ACK items 1 & 2 and post the resync-schema.json sample payload? Also: share the DPA link and confirm they support signed DPA via the link in our related_links.

Thanks — please reply with short ACKs so I can finalize the one-page playbook for onsite.

Ben Carter
Senior Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: badge-firmware-v2.1-stub.bin (firmware stub)

Hi Ben / Connor — ACK on items 1 & 2. Quick confirmations:
- We'll schedule OTA push for 2027-06-03 02:00-04:00 UTC for the 25-device pool. We'll send pre/post status webhook to the endpoint you provide.
- We'll set device resync retry window to 48h (default 72 -> reduced per request). Devices keep a circular buffer of 10k records; we recommend swapping devices expected to exceed that during staging.
- resync-schema.json (attached) shows the JSON-lines payload: each line contains {"badge_id":"...","scan_timestamp_utc":"...","email":"...","payload_checksum":"..."}. We will include consent_text and consent_method in the payload when provided by Scanner UI.
- DPA: https://badgetech.io/dpa/RDW-DPA-2027 (signed via DocuSign link on that page).

We will also provide a test device (shipped overnight) with v2.1 already installed if you confirm the ship-to address by EOD 6/1.

— BadgeTech Support
